version.value: Complete song in the original scoring for soprano and orchestra, sung in German
version.note: The fourth song is separately banded on the LP and transferred as one complete track. The published score places the orchestral prelude on pp. 44–46, the vocal stanzas on pp. 46–54, and the postlude on pp. 54–55. Hall sections and musical cues use approximate score-proportion passage timings; no bar alignment or syllable-level timing is asserted. The edition of the orchestral parts used at the session is unknown.

performers.note: All three credits appear on the original side-one label. The consulted sources do not identify the individual orchestral soloists. This is the Ackermann recording, distinct from Schwarzkopf’s later recording with George Szell.

date.note: Warner’s reissue metadata, reproduced by Presto, dates the Four Last Songs to 25 September 1953 and the accompanying Capriccio scene to 26 September. Naxos gives 25–26 September for the songs. Month-level precision retains the date on which both accounts agree; the exact day and take of Im Abendrot remain unresolved.

place.note: The Warner track documentation names Watford Town Hall. The original Angel label states Recorded in England.

label.note: The source is an original Angel vinyl LP transfer, not the later Warner or Naxos digital remaster.

catalogue.note: Internet Archive catalogues this United States release as 1954. The booklet carries the 1954 copyright notice for Edward Cushing’s English translations.

matrixTakeSides.value: Side 1, band 4; printed side matrix XAX-380; label number 1-35084
matrixTakeSides.note: XAX-380 and 1-35084 are visible on the side-one label; the track listing places Im Abendrot fourth on that side. No take number or pressing-specific runout suffix has been established.

credits.note: The institutional contributor is credited; no personal account identifier or additional restoration credit is reproduced.

processing.value: Technics SL1200MK5 turntable with Audio-Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; whole-side 24-bit FLAC transfer and segmented VBR MP3 access derivative
processing.note: The playback chain is stated in the item metadata. The whole-side FLAC is marked Processed by SoX; the selected MP3 is derived through the item’s segment data. Equalisation settings, pitch adjustment, noise reduction and other restoration decisions are unknown.

digital.format: VBR MP3 derivative of a vinyl LP transfer

composition.value: Strauss’s music and Eichendorff’s German poem are public domain under ordinary EU life-plus-70 terms.
composition.note: Strauss died in 1949 and Eichendorff in 1857. This assessment concerns Im Abendrot alone, not the three other songs’ Hermann Hesse texts. The score was first published in 1950 and remains identified by IMSLP as protected in the United States; no US composition clearance is asserted. The copyrighted English translation in the LP booklet is not reproduced.

recording.value: Territorial EU public domain under the pre-1963 commercial-publication rule: Angel 35084 was published in 1954.
recording.note: The documented 1954 lawful commercial issue predates the programme’s 1963 cutoff. Its former 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 2013 extension, which applies to recordings still protected on 1 November 2013. This is a territorial term assessment, not a Creative Commons licence or a declaration of US or worldwide public-domain status. The transferred LP, not a modern commercial remaster, supplies the audio.
